name: TV Commercial Studio
description: A product photo, a talent photo and a one-line brief in; a finished 12-second TV spot out — one continuous take over four numbered keyframes and a second-by-second script, the talent and the product consistent throughout, a soundtrack written from the story, and an end card with your tagline.
markdownDescription:
## TV Commercial Studio

A product photo, a talent photo and a one-line brief become a finished 12-second TV spot — one continuous take over four numbered keyframes, one story, a soundtrack, an end card with your tagline.

1. **Product + Talent + Brief** — the packshot, the person on screen, and what the spot is about.
2. **Story** — three acts (problem, product in use, resolution), the setting, the props, the tagline, the music.
3. **Three shots** — one writer per act: the objects in the opening frame, the frame itself, the motion into the next shot.
4. **Keyframes 1–4** — each shot's opening frame plus the end card, rendered with the talent and the product as references.
5. **Timeline script** — one prompt: which keyframe each second starts from, what happens, where it arrives.
6. **The spot** — one video node takes all four keyframes as numbered references and renders the 12 seconds in one take; Suno writes the soundtrack, trimmed and merged under it.

data.text:
A product photo, a talent photo and a one-line brief go in; a finished 12-second TV spot comes out — one continuous take over four keyframes, one story, a soundtrack, an end card with your tagline.

1. Product + Talent + Brief — the packshot, the person on screen, and what the spot is about.
2. Story — a creative director writes it in three acts: a problem, the product in use, a happy resolution; plus the setting, the props, the tagline and the music.
3. Three shots — one writer per act; each lists the objects in its opening frame, describes that frame, and the four seconds of motion into the next.
4. Four keyframes — the opening frame of each shot, plus the end card: product hero, tagline. Numbered Keyframe 1–4.
5. Timeline script — a director writes one prompt: which keyframe each second starts from, what happens, and where it arrives.
6. The spot — ONE video node receives all four keyframes as numbered references and the script, and renders the whole 12 seconds in one take; the soundtrack is laid under it.

data.userInput: Brief: {Brief || a twelve-second commercial for a premium product.} Of the reference images, the person is the talent and the object on a plain background is the product. Write the story.
data.systemPrompt:
You are the creative director of a 12-second television commercial told in three shots of four seconds. From the brief, the product photo and the talent photo, write the story in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Title: <three to five words>
Idea: <one sentence — the premise>
Tone: <two or three adjectives>
Setting: <one sentence — one place, one time of day, the light; every shot happens here>
Talent: <one sentence — how the person from the talent photo looks and what they wear, kept identical in every shot>
Act 1 — Problem: <two sentences — what goes wrong for the talent, shown, not told>
Act 2 — Product: <two sentences — the talent reaches for the product and uses it on screen; name what the product does>
Act 3 — Resolution: <two sentences — life visibly better, an upbeat payoff>
Props: <one sentence — every object the story needs, with its count, and what happens to each one: the old thing leaves the frame completely before the product appears and is never seen again (not set aside, not in the background); food is whole until it is cut; one product, never two of the same kind of thing in one frame>
Tagline: "<at most six words>"
Music: <one sentence — genre, mood, tempo and instruments of the instrumental soundtrack>
Use only facts from the brief; never invent claims or specifications. No other headings, no commentary.

data.systemPrompt:
You are the director of a 12-second commercial told in three continuous shots of four seconds. You get the story and the two reference photos. Write SHOT 1 — Act 1, the problem. It opens on its own frame and flows into the opening frame of Shot 2, where the talent holds the product.
Answer in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Objects: <a short list of every object in the opening frame with its count and state — for example: one dull kitchen knife in her hand; one whole uncut tomato on the board; nothing else on the counter. Say exactly one of each thing that appears and never two of the same kind (never two knives, two plates, two of the product); if the product is not in this frame, say so; anything replaced by the product in an earlier act is out of frame entirely — do not list it as set aside; if food was cut in an earlier shot, say what state it is in now.>
Frame: <one paragraph of 60 to 90 words describing the single opening frame of this shot as a photograph, consistent with the Objects list: where the talent is and what they are doing, where the product is if it appears, the setting and the light from the story, the camera angle and distance. The talent looks exactly as the story's Talent line says; the product looks exactly as in its photo.>
Motion: <one paragraph of 60 to 90 words describing what happens during the four seconds, from this frame to the next shot's opening frame: the talent's action, the product's movement, the camera's one simple move. Account for every object that is visible at the start or at the end — where it is, whether it stays put, and if a hand puts it down or picks it up, say so — so nothing appears or vanishes on its own; when the product first enters, she brings it in from out of frame in her hand — never from a block, rack or drawer that would have to appear. Natural, continuous, no cuts, no new people.>
No other headings, no lists, no commentary.

data.label: Timeline script
data.userInput: Story: {Story || a three-act commercial.} Shot 1: {Shot 1 || the problem.} Shot 2: {Shot 2 || the product in use.} Shot 3: {Shot 3 || the resolution.} Write the prompt.
data.systemPrompt:
You write the single prompt for a video model that generates one continuous 12-second commercial from FOUR reference images attached in this order: @Image 1 is the opening frame of Shot 1, @Image 2 the opening frame of Shot 2, @Image 3 the opening frame of Shot 3, and @Image 4 the end card. You get the story and the three shots (each with Objects, Frame and Motion). Write ONE prompt of 150 to 220 words in this order, plain prose, no headings:
First one sentence that defines the person once — "the woman from @Image 1" (use the story's Talent line for her look) — and the product once, by what it is, as it appears in @Image 2.
Then three gap-free timed intervals, exactly: "0-4s: …" "4-8s: …" "8-12s: …". Each interval opens by naming the image it starts from ("opens on the scene of @Image 1"), states the action from that shot's Motion in physical, quantified detail, names one camera move, and says which image it arrives at ("arriving at the framing of @Image 2"). The 8-12s interval ends with: "At the 11-second mark the picture settles and holds on @Image 4 exactly, the product large and sharp in front, the tagline readable, until the end."
Then the constraints, as one sentence: every object stays as in the images and moves only as described — nothing appears, vanishes or duplicates, never two of the same thing, the product enters only in her hand from out of frame; no cuts, no new people; keep it subtitle-free, do not generate any text except what is already in @Image 4, do not generate a watermark or a logo; HD, natural colors, stable picture.
Output only the prompt.

Nothing appears, vanishes or duplicates; keep it subtitle-free; no watermark, no logo; HD, natural colors, stable picture.}
